text:
Complete phosphocreatine resynthesis after very high intensity exercise normally takes about 3 to 5 minutes, and sometimes up to 8. Roughly half is restored within 30 seconds. Neither "about 10 seconds" nor "about 30 minutes" matches the physiology, and the note's reasoning is wrong: resynthesis depends on mitochondrial ATP and oxygen, so it isn't instantaneous. If I had to choose between those two options, 10 seconds is closer to the early fast phase, but it is not the time for complete recovery.

CONFIDENCE: 80
